title: A gym that pays for Starter while on Pro never moves to Starter while online buying is off
what: When HQ confirms a Starter payment for a gym still on Pro or in its trial, the gym is told Starter starts on the day Pro ends. Only the nightly billing job makes that switch, and that job runs only when online buying is switched on, which it is not. So the gym stays on Pro for ever at the Starter price, and its admin app keeps showing a Starter start date that has passed.
expected: The planned switch to Starter happens on its day whether or not online buying is on.
who: gym owners who choose Starter, and MettleUp
how_often: every Starter payment confirmed for a gym on Pro or trial
fix_line: Run the planned plan switch every night on its own, not only when online buying is on.

title: Leads, help questions and replies, AI limits and the online-payment settings have no backup and no restore steps
what: The nightly backup copies only the gym server. The second, smaller database holds the website leads, every feedback and help message with your replies, each gym's AI limits, the online-payment records and switches, and HQ's messages to gyms. It is in no copy, and the written restore steps never mention it. If that database or the Cloudflare account were lost, all of it would be gone.
expected: Every database MettleUp keeps is in the nightly copy, or the written restore steps say how to bring it back.
how_often: only if that database or account is lost
fix_line: Add the second database to the nightly copy, or write down how to bring it back from Cloudflare's own history.

title: HQ opens for one Google account only, and there is no written way back in if it is lost
what: HQ lets in only the one Google address kept as a secret on Cloudflare. If that Google account, or the laptop holding its passkey, is lost, the only way back is to change that secret and send HQ out again from a computer signed in to Cloudflare. HQ is never sent out by GitHub, only by hand, and nothing in HQ's setup names a second person or the steps to follow.
expected: A written, tested way back into HQ and Cloudflare that does not depend on one laptop or one Google account.
how_often: only if the Google account or laptop is lost
fix_line: Write the way back in (who, which accounts, which steps) and keep a second trusted sign-in or recovery set.

title: If the nightly clean-up or billing job fails, nobody is told
what: The nightly backup and the direct-read record each have a status the watch reads and turns into an alert. The nightly clean-up (old feedback, old leads, old AI requests, test gyms) and the nightly billing job only write a hidden log line when they fail. The deletions the privacy notice promises could stop for weeks without you knowing.
expected: A failed nightly clean-up or billing run shows up the same way a failed backup does.
who: you, and members whose old data should be deleted
fix_line: Save the result of each nightly job and let the watch alert on a failure, like the backup.

title: The key behind staff browser alerts is kept in one place only, and HQ says it must never change
what: The key that sends gym alerts to staff browsers is made once, never shown, and stored only as a Cloudflare secret. The setup note says never change it, because every browser's alerts are tied to it. There is no copy, so if HQ is ever made again or moved to another account, every staff browser stops getting alerts until each one signs up again.
expected: A safe copy of the key is kept with the other recovery items, or the admin app signs browsers up again by itself when the key changes.
how_often: only if HQ is re-made or moved
fix_line: Keep a sealed copy of the alert key, or make browsers sign up again when the key changes.
